annotations.title: Find a vault by what it has done

description: Find a vault by what it has DONE rather than what it is called. Free. The filter worth knowing is `earned`: `short` returns the vaults where a holder earned LESS than the venue advertises — how many there are is in the answer, never here — and `beating` the ones where they earned more. It matches on the same verdict vault_check leads with, `delivery.verdict`, over a comparable period (each row carries it as `earnedVerdict` with its days and basis); never on the ratio to today’s quote, which is context. It matches only vaults with such a verdict, which is a SMALL part of the open vaults and the exact share is in `vaults_earned`, not in this sentence; a venue that quotes nothing or a share price that never moves is excluded rather than counted as in-line, so a short list here means few comparable and not few that performed. Call vault_check on a slug for the full answer.

agentManaged.description: Only vaults whose venue DECLARES autonomous agents run them: a platform built for it, one in DefiLlama’s AI Agents category, or a hand-checked operator declaration. A claim, not verified. Execution timing alone does not qualify.

allDimensionsRead.description: Send `true` for the strict filter: no known severe finding AND every dimension read. noSevere=true alone is "no known severe" (severeCheck.label no_known_severe) and keeps vaults with dimensions we did not read.

asset.description: The underlying token symbol as read, e.g. USDC. Vaults whose asset was never read are excluded and counted in warnings, never treated as matching.

automatedExecution.description: Software at work in execution, declared or inferred from reallocation timing. Not evidence that an AI decides.

depositsOpen.description: true: only vaults taking deposits now, as read; false: only those closed to deposits. Unread deposit states are excluded and counted.

earned.description: in-line, beating or short: the verdict over a comparable period, the same one vault_check gives as delivery.verdict; each row carries it as earnedVerdict.

flag.description: book_value_not_shown_recoverable or no_withdrawable_liquidity: only vaults carrying that critical flag.

includeUnknown.description: With noSevere=true, send `true` to also get vaults whose severe check could not be completed, each marked `severeCheck.state: unknown`.

includeUnreadLenses.description: With any of the newer-reading filters above: also return vaults never measured on one, each marked unknown in `screenEvidence.lenses.verdicts`.

instantExit.description: true: only vaults a holder leaves synchronously, as read from the contract or documented by the venue (screenEvidence.lenses.exitMechanicSource). Request-and-claim or a queue fails; a mechanic never read is unknown.

largestHolderIdentified.description: true: only vaults whose largest holder read is named by a source (known infrastructure such as a confidential wrapper, an operator address book, our vault index, an explorer tag). An address nobody names fails; a vault with no holder book is unknown and counted apart.

limit.description: Default 25, capped at 100, or 1000 with export.bulk; meta.limit says what was applied and what held it. Above 1000 is refused with 400, never cut.

maxAgeHours.description: Only vaults whose size was read within this many hours.

maxFinalBand.description: Ceiling on the final band, after the credit-chain overlay. A vault with no published band is excluded.

maxModelScore.description: Ceiling on the base model score ONLY. Does not read the credit overlay, the final band or any finding: a row can carry a severe final band. Use maxRisk or maxFinalBand to screen for low risk.

maxReportAgeHours.description: Only vaults whose due-diligence report is at most this old. A vault with no report does not pass.

maxRisk.description: Ceiling on the published risk score in the stored due-diligence report, AND on the final band: a vault within the score whose final band (after the credit-chain overlay) or highest known finding reads worse than the band of the ceiling is EXCLUDED and listed in the warning `max_risk_reads_final_band`. Withheld, unavailable and report-less vaults are EXCLUDED, which is not the same as scoring well, and the counts are on the answer rather than here. A vault whose report result is not usable for a current decision (dueDiligence.assessment.usableForCurrentDecision false) is EXCLUDED too and listed in `not_usable_never_passes_a_ceiling`: its score is a historical computation, not a clearance. Each row shows `screenEvidence.riskLayers` (base model, credit overlay, final band, highest known finding) and `screenEvidence.publishedRisk`.

maxTop1Share.description: Ceiling on the largest address’s share of the holders we read, 0 to 1 (capital quality, vaults of $1M or more). A vault not read is left out and counted in the warning `lens_filters`, never as failing. An address is not an owner.

maxUnidentifiedHolderShare.description: Ceiling, 0 to 1, on the largest share of the vault any address no source names holds, among its largest holders read. No holder book: unknown, counted apart.

minDelivery.description: Floor on realised over advertised (e.g. 0.8), read only where the comparison is comparable; every other vault is unknown.

minDepositCapacityUsd.description: Only vaults whose contract would accept at least this many dollars at the last reading, for an address with no special standing. Not a promise the transaction goes through.

minHoldersToEmpty.description: Floor on how many of the largest holders we read must leave first before today’s instant exit is empty (exit window; a scenario, not a forecast). A queue exit has no instant exit and is unknown.

minOwnShare.description: Floor on the share of the vault its leader holds, 0 to 1. Readable on Hyperliquid and Drift only, so a floor on it excludes every other venue, where it is ABSENT and not zero. How many that is today is in the answer. Evidence of alignment, never proof: the holder can be a treasury or a custodian.

minRetention30.description: Floor on the share of arriving capital whose address was still in after 30 days, 0 to 1 (capital quality). Not read: left out and counted apart.

minTvl.description: Floor on stated size, in US dollars.

noCollateralBreak.description: true: leave out vaults whose material tokenized-stock or stablecoin collateral breaks from its reference on a live reading. With the exchange closed the reading is unknown, not holding.

noImpairedBook.description: true: leave out vaults marked as book value in markets Morpho flags RED (50% or more of the allocation). A vault whose allocation was not read is unknown, not clean.

noSevere.description: Send `true` to get only vaults whose severe check PASSES: their due-diligence headline was read and nothing in it is severe (each row carries `severeCheck`: pass | fail | unknown; a vault with no headline is unknown and left out unless includeUnknown=true). `maxRisk` alone does not: it is the weighted model result. Applied to up to the 3,000 largest matches; `meta.pagination.rowFilterScope.complete` says whether every candidate was examined, and where it is false `total` counts matches among the examined only.

offset.description: Where to start, for the next page: send the `nextOffset` of the previous answer. Default 0.

operator.description: The operator or curator slug, as operator_check takes it.

platform.description: A platform id or its display name, e.g. morpho or Hyperliquid.

q.description: Part of a name or an address.

screenedNoHit.description: true: only vaults whose sanctions screening (OFAC SDN, exact address match over roles, the vault contract, controlling addresses and direct holders) is complete, has no match and is at most 7 days old. An exact match fails; a partial, stale or never-run screening is unknown, never a failure. Each row says the screening’s age in screenEvidence.lenses.sanctionsAgeHours.

name: find_vaults

data.description: Each with its slug, which vault_check takes.

fields.description: Which fields this tool kept from the endpoint’s own rows.

meta.description: How current this answer is and what it was read from: `freshness` and the ages behind it. Present on every answer from this server, whatever the tool.

warnings.description: Anything the server wants a caller to know about THIS answer before acting on it, each {code, message, says} with message and says the same sentence. Empty is the normal case and is not a guarantee.
